title: OverflowTabs
summary: A tab strip with more tabs than fit is the MonarchTabs: the tabs that do not fit scroll sideways, and the selected tab is brought into view. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For five or more sections of one screen, or tabs whose labels are long or translated, where a fixed MonarchTabs would squeeze them.
whenNotToUse: For two to four short sections, use MonarchTabs, which fills the width (see tabs). For top-level destinations, use the navigation bar or rail (see app-shell). For a long list of views, use a dropdown menu.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTabs(selectedIndex: Int, onSelectedIndexChange: (Int) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, panel: (@Composable (selectedIndex: Int) -> Unit)? = null, tabs: MonarchTabsScope.() -> Unit)

interface MonarchTabsScope { fun tab(text: String, enabled: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable () -> Unit)? = null, count: String? = null, countTone: MonarchTone = MonarchTone.Neutral, contentDescription: String? = null) }

states.name: fits
states.description: All tabs are visible, packed from the start with the edge padding.

states.name: overflowing
states.description: The row scrolls sideways; the tabs at the end are reached by swiping.

states.name: selected out of view
states.description: Selecting a tab, or setting selectedTabIndex from code, scrolls it into view.

appearance: The tab row uses the colors Monarch maps to the Material scheme: the canvas surface, the accent color for the selected tab's text and indicator, the muted text color for the others and a subtle divider. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web OverflowTabs measures the strip and moves the last tabs into a More menu as the width shrinks. On Android the scrolling tab row is the platform pattern: every tab stays one swipe away and nothing is measured. When the extra tabs should sit in a menu instead, compose a MonarchTabs of the first tabs with a last Tab that opens a MonarchMenu. The web's TabsContent panels are the app's own content switched on the selected index. iOS documents a recipe on MonarchTabs, which also scrolls.
accessibility: System behavior: each Tab has the tab role and its selected state; TalkBack reads "Tab, 3 of 8" with the row as a collection.
Each tab has a touch target of at least 48dp.
Tabs scrolled out of view are still reached by TalkBack, which scrolls the row as it moves.
The selected tab is marked by the indicator and its color, and by the selected state for TalkBack.
edgeCases: Labels do not wrap: a very long label makes a wide tab; keep them to one or two words.
At large font sizes fewer tabs fit and more scroll.

examples.title: Wide
examples.template:
MonarchTabs(
    selectedIndex = selected,
    onSelectedIndexChange = { selected = it },
    panel = { index -> MonarchText(text = "${titles[index]} content") },
) {
        tab({{tabs.0.label}})
        tab({{tabs.1.label}}, count = "{{tabs.1.count|raw}}", countTone = {{tabs.1.countTone|tone}})
        tab({{tabs.2.label}})
        tab({{tabs.3.label}})
        tab({{tabs.4.label}})
        tab({{tabs.5.label}}, enabled = !{{tabs.5.disabled}})
        tab({{tabs.6.label}})
        tab({{tabs.7.label}})
}
examples.setupTemplate:
var selected by remember { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
val titles = listOf({{tabs.0.label}}, {{tabs.1.label}}, {{tabs.2.label}}, {{tabs.3.label}}, {{tabs.4.label}}, {{tabs.5.label}}, {{tabs.6.label}}, {{tabs.7.label}})
examples.setup:
var selected by remember { mutableIntStateOf(0) }
val titles = listOf("Overview", "Activity", "Files", "Members", "Integrations", "Billing", "Audit log", "Settings")
examples.code:
MonarchTabs(
    selectedIndex = selected,
    onSelectedIndexChange = { selected = it },
    panel = { index -> MonarchText(text = "${titles[index]} content") },
) {
        tab("Overview")
        tab("Activity", count = "4", countTone = MonarchTone.Accent)
        tab("Files")
        tab("Members")
        tab("Integrations")
        tab("Billing", enabled = !true)
        tab("Audit log")
        tab("Settings")
}

parityExceptions.reason: NATIVE GAP: The tab strip has an accessible name (Workspace sections) and selects the tab by value (overview); the Android tab row takes no label and selects by index
